00DE60  func  animate_step_with_flags  # steps of two words: flags (into sprite_flags bits 6-7, the flips) and frame
00DEFD  func  animate_and_move         # steps of frame, dx, dy: projected_x/projected_y move by dx/dy (negated by the flips)
00DF72  func  animate_around_anchor    # steps of frame, dx, dy: projected position = anchor + dx/dy (set_step_around_anchor)
00DFC1  func  set_step_around_anchor   # projected_x = anchor_x + dx, projected_y = anchor_y + dy (negated by the flips)
00DFF5  func  animate_with_screen_offset   # steps of frame, dx, dy added to screen_x/screen_y (add_step_screen_offset)
00E049  func  apply_step_screen_offset # the current step's dx/dy again without advancing (animate_with_screen_offset between steps)
00E058  func  add_step_screen_offset   # screen_x += dx, screen_y += dy of the step at R10 (negated by the flips)

# ======== collisions between objects ========
# Objects put themselves in lists while they run; the stage's mode routine (095177, also 000652 and
# 09492F) tests the lists in the next frame before run_objects (check_zones, check_hits, check_walls,
# check_platforms), sets flags bits and partner fields on both objects of each pair, and empties the
# lists. Lists are 16-bit addresses ending with FFFF.
20F07E  var   hitter_list  u16 object         # objects that test themselves against every touchable object and each other: the players (00B5BA) and 011EAB; through hit_list_next
20F080  var   touchable_list  u16 object      # objects the hitters can touch (rings, enemies, items: 77 handlers call add_to_touchable_list)
20E5F0  var   zone_list  u16 object           # objects whose box the hitters' x/y is tested against (check_zones; 010AD7, 080372, 082ED3...)
20F090  var   rider_list  u16 object          # objects that can stand on platforms and enter areas (the players, rings...); through platform_list_next
20F092  var   platform_list  u16 object       # platforms (085F80, 087FA5, 08815E...)
0020A5  func  add_to_hitter_list       # pushes R20 on hitter_list; clears flags bits 2 and 27
0020C2  func  add_to_touchable_list    # pushes R20 on touchable_list; clears flags bits 2 and 6
001956  func  add_to_zone_list         # pushes R20 on zone_list; clears flags bit 27
0020DB  func  add_to_rider_list        # pushes R20 on rider_list; clears flags bits 3 and 5
0020F4  func  add_to_platform_list     # pushes R20 on platform_list; clears flags bit 3
001DDD  func  check_hits               # every hitter against the hitters after it and, if it is not touched yet, against touchable_list; empties both lists
001E33  func  check_hit                # R17 against the list from R10: skips pairs where both kinds are 0-2; in x/y box/box, box/round (the round one as a square of its radius), point/box or circle/circle (radii summed, slope-corrected); then the heights; a hit sets flags bit 2 on both, touched_by to each other, 6C = a coordinate from the test (R2)
0018B6  func  check_zones              # every hitter whose x/y is inside a zone object's box with the heights overlapping: flags bit 27 on both, anchor_x = each other; empties zone_list
002108  func  check_platforms          # every rider whose x/y is inside a platform's box (no offsets): rider flags bit 3, platform fields of both; the platform also gets bit 3 when the rider's z is not above its floor_z (56), and the first time adds its 6F to the lists at 209400/209500 (sorted by 0021F9); empties both lists
00B5BA  func  add_player_to_lists      # add_to_hitter_list then add_to_rider_list (the player handlers)
00B5C6  func  remember_platform        # flags bit 4 = bit 3 (was on a platform)
01F0EF  func  check_left_screen        # R8 = -1 once an object that has been on screen (flags bit 11) is out of it by 0x20; sets bit 11 while it is inside
01F141  func  check_left_screen_margin # the same with the margin in R1
01F18C  func  check_left_screen_margins   # margin R1 once seen, R2 before
01F091  func  is_off_screen            # R8 = -1 when screen_x + 0x20 >= 0x180 or screen_y + 0x20 >= 0x120
01F0BC  func  is_off_screen_margin     # the same with margins R1 (x) and R3 (y)

# ======== shadows and the rings the generic code makes ========
01EF99  func  draw_child_shadow        # puts the child (pool 2, frame 5D90) at the floor under the object (projected_y + floor_z, sprite offsets), palette 9FFE, or 87A0 every other frame when flags bit 4; queues it at its screen_y - 0x10 (behind the object)
01E709  func  scatter_rings            # R8 rings (at most 10) at the current object: kind 3, flags 0x204 (bit 9 for the first 0x1E frames), speed/direction/jump (random unless 20F0EA says so), a pool 2 shadow each, handler scattered_ring_wait
01E701  func  scatter_rings_random     # 20F0EA = 0: random direction, speed and jump for each ring (00F8E1, drop_rings)
01E6F7  func  scatter_rings_fixed      # 20F0EA = FFFF (0826CE; unreached)
01E85B  func  scattered_ring_wait      # handler: 7E counts down with flags bit 9 set, then scattered_ring_live
01E86E  func  scattered_ring_live      # handler: 80 counts 0x12C frames, then the ring shrinks away; touched: taken (sound 13, 01EA86, deleted with its shadow) unless the player is in state D/20 with C3 set
01E8C8  func  move_scattered_ring      # moves on x/y (steps back and turns round when the floor rises more than 8), gravity 0x6000, bounces keeping 3/4 of speed_z, animates; out of the screen (is_off_screen_margin 0x20/0x58) it switches to scattered_ring_vanish
01E9C1  func  scattered_ring_vanish    # handler: ring and shadow sprite_scale - 0x10 a frame, then deleted
01EEC2  func  next_random              # reads two words through the random number area at D80000 (position 20F0FC, moved on by each value); R3 = the result

# ======== players (from build/naming/players.txt) ========
# Naming proposals: THE PLAYERS (struct player, the player handlers and state machine, player globals)
# Format: symbols.txt syntax, one proposal per line, "# evidence" after it.
# Conventions used below: "p" is the player number (OBJECT->player, 0-2); "the object" is the player's object
# (struct player +14 points at it, the object's 9C points back at the block).
#
# ======== struct player (0x200 bytes from 0x208400, R18 = current_player) ========
field player 00 state u8                    # 002CEC jumps through the table at 002D3E (58 entries) and 002FF1 through 002FFC; values below
field player 01 facing u8                   # 16-way sprite direction: ((facing_angle + 0x20) >> 6) & 0xF (00BD2C); indexes every animation table by 2 x facing
field player 03 substate u8                 # step inside a state (AT8(unk_02, 1) in the C): states switch on it, reset to 0 on most state changes
field player 04 state_timer s16             # per-state countdown/counter: 0x3C on a ledge (state 5), 0x1E/0x14/6 hurt and bounce, 0x168 goal run, +1 in state 0x24
field player 06 control_lock u8             # frames the trackball is ignored: counts down in the normal states (002DEC); 00B90A runs only when 0; set 4/0xA after bounces, 0x10/0x7F/0xFF in scripted states
field player 07 jump_delay s8               # 00B60A: counts down, the button is only checked (00B62D) when it reaches 0; 1 after a jump, 2 after being pushed out of an object
field player 08 standing_started u8         # 0030AD: 0xFF the frame the standing animation starts (long first frame); frames then last 3, except 2 and 6
field player 09 is_joining u8               # 0xFF from the credit (states 0xB/0x23/0x24) until the join sequence 00E1A9 ends; 001D07 then starts the object at 0028DB
field player 0A trackball_x s16             # 00BDCE: this player's trackball_N_x (0x20F062 + 4p) & ~1, shifted left 8 (trace: dx 11 -> 0x0A00)
field player 0C trackball_y s16             # 00BDCE: the same from trackball_N_y (0x20F064 + 4p) (trace: dy -4 -> -0x400)
field player 0E invulnerable_timer s16      # 002CEC decrements it every frame and stops at -1; >= 0 ignores hazards (00E488); 600 while hurt, 120 after a hurt or a respawn; blinks via object 30 bit 29 (00B5DC)
field player 12 heading u16                 # angle (0-0x3FF) the player moves toward; turns toward target_heading at a limited rate (00BC50)
field player 14 object u16 object                  # 002808: the player's object (low 16 bits); 001A7F, 00BED5, 015F80, 0983FE read it
field player 1A last_hazard u16             # 00E488: object that last hurt the player; a hit from another object restarts the hurt substate
field player 1C scene_hop_z s32             # state 0x18 scene step 6: height added to z while the character hops in place (speed_z per character)
field player 20 ledge_pullback s16          # 00B361: trackball movement back toward the floor while teetering (state 5) or slipping (7); >= 0x10/0x14 recovers
field player 22 ledge_side s16              # 00B3AC: side of the floor block the player went off (0-3), 4 = still inside; -1 when unused
field player 24 slip_distance s32           # state 7: += speed every frame; ends the slide at 0x20000000 (0x8000000 on floor type 9)
field player 28 target_heading u16          # angle from the trackball (00BBEC, 00B2C0) or the autopilot path (00DCC5); heading follows it
field player 2C climb_remaining s16         # state 0xA: height left to the top of the wall (0 = climb over, table +6 = back at the bottom); state 0x27: the x that ends the climb (object 94)
field player 2E climb_from_top u8           # state 0xA: 0xFF when the player reached the wall at or above its top (climbs down; falls if it came jumping)
field player 2F hit_stop u8                 # 00E488 sets 3 when the jump takes the enemy's health to 0 (sturdy kinds excepted; otherwise the player bounces off); while nonzero the player does not move (002EF7)
field player 30 step_accumulator s32        # state 0xA: speed_y summed, +-4 climbs one step; state 0x27 (008AD2): speed summed in the high word, 0x400 = one step
field player 34 screen_x s32                # 16.16 screen x used when the code places the sprite directly: climbing, dying (0x16), scenes 0x18/0x1C, riding (0x27)
field player 36 screen_x_int s16        # the whole part of screen_x
field player 38 in_game s8                  # 1 while the player has a game going (credit used), 0 when out; 002953 respawns only when > 0
field player 3C skid_slowdown s32           # state 0xC: ground_speed / 8 (/32 on floor type 7), subtracted every frame
field player 40 skid_speed_slowdown s32     # state 0xC: object speed (6E) / 8 (/32 on floor type 7), subtracted every frame until 0
field player 46 free_turn_timer u8          # counts down in the normal states; while nonzero 00BC50 sets heading = target_heading at once (no skid)
field player 48 skid_dust_timer s8          # state 0xC: a dust puff (00A669) every 4 frames
field player 49 bounce_direction u8         # state 0xE: 0-3, picks the bounce animation (table 1139E8 + 6 x dir); set by 00C920/00E488 (as a 16-bit write that also hits 4A)
field player 4A bounce_speed_z s32          # state 0xE and 0x1D: the bounce animation advances a frame each time speed_z passes it; += bounce_step
field player 4E bounce_step s32             # state 0xE: step added to bounce_speed_z (0x34000, then 2/3 of the rebound)
field player 52 previous_state u8           # saved before a forced state (stage events, ledges, scenes) and restored by them
field player 53 ignore_screen_edges u8      # 00AD91 does not push the player back from the screen edges while set (only cleared, in 0029DF)
field player 5C path_pointer u32 rom            # 00DCC5: current record of the autopilot path (ROM 115528): +0 speed, +2 x, +4 y, +6 flags (bit 0 jump), 8 bytes each
field player 64 ground_speed s32            # 16.16 speed along heading after the slope tables (00B90A, 00BD5F); 00C4AD turns it into speed_x/speed_y
field player 68 walk_cycle s16              # walking: += animation_speed >> 16 every frame; each 0x200 the walk animation steps and the pending movement is applied
field player 6A walk_pending_x s32          # state 1 at low speed: speed_x summed and added to x only on animation steps (002EB0)
field player 6E walk_pending_y s32          # the same for y
field player 72 attack_power s8             # set to 4 when a jump starts (constant in this build; sound 0x1F); subtracted from the enemy's health (object 7E) in 00E488
field player 75 joined_health_setting u8    # 002808: copy of health_setting at join; indexes the max health table 113EF2 (00E488)
field player 76 previous_x s32              # x before this frame's movement; restored when blocked (00B6AC, 00C920, 00E488)
field player 7A previous_y s32              # the same for y
field player 7E previous_z s32              # the same for z (height)
field player 84 screen_edge u16             # 00AD91: which screen edge (0-3) pushes the player back; indexes 113EE0 and 113CE7
field player 86 hud_portrait u16 object            # 00A6EE: address of this block's portrait sprite record (+0x172)
field player 88 hud_gauge u16 object               # 00A6EE: address of this block's health gauge sprite record (+0x142)
field player 8A heading_snapped u16         # 00BD0B: heading rounded to 16 directions; object 24 gets it + 0x80
field player 94 push_x s16                  # 00DA9B: floor push (table 10E14C + 7A) or quicksand pull (00E488 kind 28); added to the trackball in 00B90A
field player 96 push_y s16                  # the same for y
field player 98 animation_speed s32         # smoothed trackball speed: 0 -> standing, < 0x200 walking (1), else running (0x13), > 0x4F0 running fast (0x14) (00B90A)
field player 9C holder u16 object                  # state 0x15: the object (kind 8/10) holding the player; set in 00E488
field player A0 pushed_out s8               # 00E488 kind 5/12/32/33: 0xFF while the player is stuck in a solid object and being pushed out
field player A1 push_out_delay s8           # 00E488: 0x1E frames against the same solid object before pushing out
field player A2 push_out_x s32              # 00CCB0: push-out speed toward the screen centre
field player A6 push_out_y s32              # the same for y
field player AA fall_draw_depth u16         # states 6-9: sprite sort key while falling into a pit (floor screen y, adjusted by floor block type)
field player AC jump_first_tile u16         # state 4: first sprite of the jump animation; gravity applies once the animation leaves it
field player B0 path_speed u16              # 00DCC5: speed of the current path record (0 = wait path_wait frames)
field player B2 path u8                     # 00DCC5: autopilot path being followed (0 = trackball control); the trackball is ignored while set
field player B4 mishap_flag u8              # 0xFF when hurt, falling into a pit, joining...; 001A7F turns any of them into 20E5A3 and clears all three
field player B5 saved_substate u8           # 002F46: substate kept when a floor type forces a new state
field player B6 facing_angle u16            # angle the sprite faces (from the trackball, 00BBEC); facing = 16-way version
field player B8 scene_step_seen u8          # states 0x18/0x19/0x1C/0x1E: last scene_step handled, so each step runs its setup once
field player B9 path_request u8             # path to start (00DCC5 copies it into path): 0x14 intro run, 5, 0xE, 0x2F, 0x4D, 0x50, 0x53, exit paths
field player BA scene_zoom s32              # states 0x18/0x1C: drives the object's zoom (08) in the stage scenes
field player BE hud_blink_timer s8          # 00AD0D: 0x1E frames per blink of the player's HUD message
field player BF hud_blink_on u8             # 00AD0D: toggles; draws or erases the message
field player C0 path_wait s16               # 00DCC5: frames to wait at a path record with speed 0
field player C2 entry_status u8             # 002BC5/00D2BA: 0xFF playing, 0x81 dropping in from above, 0x82 waiting for the stage; copied to player_status[p]
field player C3 hurt_contact_delay s8       # states 0xD/0x20: frames before 00E488 checks contacts again (2 after a hit, 0xA/0x78 at start)
field player C4 speed_scale u16             # 00D2A7: target speed x speed_scale / 16 when nonzero; the pacing object 0843D5 sets 0xD on one player by position
field player C6 last_damaged u16            # 00E488: enemy last hit by the jump; the same enemy is not hit twice in a row
field player C8 escape_progress s32         # trackball shaking toward breaking free: states 0x1D (007834), 0x25 step 12, 0x32
field player CC draw_depth u16              # sprite sort key passed to 099FC0 (floor screen y): 0030AD, 0032DD, 00D22E
field player CE side_step_accumulator s32   # state 0xA: speed_x summed, +-2 moves one step along the wall
field player D2 saved_screen_x s32          # state 0xA: screen_x before the last step, restored by 00E488 when the step is blocked
field player D6 saved_screen_y s32          # state 0xA: object 2C before the last step
field player DA saved_climb_remaining u16   # state 0xA: climb_remaining before the last step
field player DC goal_step u8                # state 0x21 (stage exit): 0 start the exit path, 1 walking it, 2 done
field player DD effect_spawned u8           # state 0x22: the effect (084BBA type 0xB) was already started
field player E0 last_wall u16               # 00B6AC: wall (object 78, list 20F0AE) that last pushed the player back
field player E2 wall_timer s8               # 00B6AC: 0x1E frames of being pushed back by the same wall
field player E3 drift_anim_step u8          # 0096F1: animation step while carried by the scroll (states 0x25/0x26)
field player E4 continue_frames s8          # state 0x23: frames of the current second (60; the button jumps to the next)
field player E5 continue_seconds s8         # state 0x23: 9 down to 0, drawn by 099A57; at 0 the game is over (0x2E)
field player EA sequence_step u8            # step of the long scripted states 0x25 and 0x31 (they do not use substate)
field player EB ledge_direction s8          # when ledge_side is 4: side from the floor block's slope (0-3); 00D7E8, states 5/9/0x33
field player EC struggle_speed u16          # floor type 0xA: trackball speed >> 16; slows the sinking (00CE7B)
field player EE sink_depth s16              # quicksand: += 0x33 a frame (00CE08, 00CE7B), z = floor + sink_depth << 8; 0x2000 costs 8 health
field player F4 ground_clip_bottom u16      # clip record at +0xF0 (8 words from 002808: 0x5000, 0xE0, 0, 0x140): its bottom gets the ground's screen y so a sinking player is cut there
field player 114 flags u32                  # bit0 drawn clipped at the ground (shadow_update, sinking floors), bit1 on a kind 29 object (edges drop at once, 00B3E7), bit2 sinking in quicksand, bit3 no shadow (exit done), bit4 just joined, bit5 edge voice played, bit6 ring this frame, bit7 jumped into a pit
field player 118 swirl_turn_rate u16        # state 0x28: divisor of the turn toward the object at 20E5D4 (0x220)
field player 11E object_climb_steps u16     # state 0x27: 1 at the start, +1 per step; the draw depth uses it
field player 120 climb_hand s8               # state 0x27, character 1: 0xFF and 1 alternate (which hand); 0 for the others
field player 11D enter_on_respawn u8        # 0029DF: 0xFF in a game after a stage start; 00CFCA then runs the walk-in state 0x2A (if the stage has a path)
field player 122 entry_step u8              # state 0x2A: 0 start the entry path, 1 wait for it to end
field player 123 hud_message_shown u8       # 00A8E9: the "joining closed" message was drawn (cleared when it is erased)
field player 124 jump_frames s16            # state 4: frames since the jump started; > 0x50 ends it
field player 126 hud_ring_effect u16        # 00A6EE: address of this block's ring effect sprite record (+0x1A2)
field player 128 scene_path u8              # 00D026: path started when scene_step reaches 1 or 8 in state 0x18 (0xB or 0x11 in stage 5)
field player 129 ending_step u8             # state 0x38: step of the stage 0xB sequence
field player 12A edge_object u16 object            # 00B3E7: object of a moving edge (floor block type 0x10, floor type 1); state 7 compares positions with it
field player 12E fast_climb u8              # state 0xA: 0xFF on floor block type 0x20 above z 0x4DE; steps need 4 x the input
field player 130 climb_base_z s32           # state 0xA: floor height at the foot of the wall
field player 134 ending_done u8             # state 0x38: set at the end; 00D637 does not start it again
field player 135 game_over_done u8          # state 0x2E waits for 08EC87 to set it, then goes to 0x24
field player 137 stages_reached u8          # 1 when joining, +1 per stage exit (state 0x21; not after stages 5, 0xB-0xF) and in state 0x2B; 08EAC9 copies it to the ranking record
field player 138 ridden_object u16          # state 0x35: object the player rides (from 00E149)
field player 13A rings u16                  # +1 per ring (00E488 kinds 3/42), drawn in the HUD in decimal (00A8E9), the ranking score (08EAC9), +200 in state 0x2B; 0 when joining
field player 13C stage_rings u16            # +1 per ring, 0 at each stage start (00291F); 0983FE adds the three for the stage result percentage
field player 13E splash_zone u8             # state 0xA on floor block type 0x20: 0xFF while z is in 0x4C7-0x4E9; entering it calls 00E263
field player 13F was_in_splash_zone u8      # previous frame's splash_zone
field player 141 rings_to_health s8         # 00E488: rings since the last health point (1 health per 4 or 8 rings with some settings)
field player 144 hud_gauge_flags u16        # health gauge sprite record at +0x142 (object layout): +02
field player 146 hud_gauge_tile u16         # +04 (0x89E0)
field player 148 hud_gauge_palette u16      # +06
field player 14E hud_gauge_y u16            # +0C screen y (table 113F10/113F1C per player)
field player 150 hud_gauge_x u16            # +0E screen x
field player 166 hud_gauge_health u8        # +24: health shown; a drop flashes the gauge (00A8E9)
field player 168 hud_gauge_anim_delay u8    # +26
field player 16A hud_gauge_anim u32         # +28: palette animation (0xCD4D hit, 0xCD37 ring, 0xCD55 low health)
field player 16E hud_gauge_anim_repeats u8  # +2C: loops left of the palette animation (00ACA1)
field player 16F hud_gauge_reset u8         # +2D: 0xFF while the player is not playing; 00A8E9 resets the HUD animations when it is cleared
field player 174 hud_portrait_flags u16     # portrait sprite record at +0x172: +02
field player 176 hud_portrait_tile u16      # +04 (per character, table 113F38)
field player 178 hud_portrait_palette u16   # +06
field player 17E hud_portrait_y u16         # +0C (table 113F24/113F30 per player)
field player 180 hud_portrait_x u16         # +0E
field player 197 hud_portrait_frame u8      # +25
field player 198 hud_portrait_anim_delay u8 # +26
field player 19A hud_portrait_anim u32      # +28: 0xCD63/6B/73 hurt, 0xCD7B/89/97 low health, per character
field player 19E hud_portrait_anim_repeats u8  # +2C
field player 1A4 hud_ring_effect_flags u16  # ring effect sprite record at +0x1A2: +02
field player 1A8 hud_ring_effect_palette u16  # +06
field player 1AE hud_ring_effect_y u16      # +0C (next to the gauge)
field player 1B0 hud_ring_effect_x u16      # +0E
field player 1C7 hud_ring_effect_frame u8   # +25: restarted (0) when a ring is collected, 0xFF when the animation ends (00A8E9, 00ACD6)
field player 1C8 hud_ring_effect_anim_delay u8  # +26
field player 1CA hud_ring_effect_anim u32   # +28
field player 1D2 join_time u32              # 00E1A9: frame counter 20F050 when the player joined; record_player_game (09FB3B) subtracts it (play time)
field player 1D6 last_scroll u16            # 00E415: stage scroll (20E435) seen last frame
field player 1D8 stall_frames s16           # 00E415: frames the scroll has not moved; 7200 (2 minutes) sets health to 0 and state 0xD (not in stage 5)
#
# Player states (field player 00). Main table at 002D3E (002CEC), animation table at 002FFC (002FF1); the
# code labels below name each state's entry.
#   00 standing (00B90A: no input)                 01 walking (animation_speed below 0x200)
#   02 falling to a lower floor (00C920)            03 inactive: the handler returns at once (no setter found)
#   04 jumping, the attack (button, 00B62D)         05 teetering at a pit edge (slow): pull back to recover, else 06
#   06 falling off the edge into the pit            07 over an edge at speed or jumping into a pit: slides, hangs on; pull back to climb up, else 08
#   08 dropping from the edge into the pit          09 falling into a pit from the air (00B465)
#   0A climbing a wall (floor type 2)               0B not playing: waits for a credit and the start button
#   0C skidding (turn of 90 degrees or more at speed, 00BC50)  0D hurt (-4 health, knocked back, invulnerable)
#   0E bouncing off a wall or an object at speed    0F launched by a bumper (kinds 6/7), bouncing to a stop
#   10 the same as 0F, from floor type 3            11, 12 the same code as 0F (no setter found)
#   13 running                                      14 running fast (animation_speed above 0x4F0)
#   15 held by an object (kind 8/10 caught while jumping) until it lets go
#   16 dying (health 0): flies off the screen, then 0x23
#   17 hopping (floor type 6, or released by a holder)
#   18 stage 0 / stage 5 scene (00D026): paths, poses and zoom by scene_step
#   19 thrown by the game mode 0x0D event (stage 8), by scene_step
#   1A inactive (returns at once)                   1B one 65-frame animation, then standing (no setter found)
#   1C opening scene of the first stage (game mode 0x10, 00D2BA)
#   1D stuck in an object (kind 17): shake the trackball to escape
#   1E game intro (mode 1): waits for its character's turn (intro_character), then runs path 0x14
#   1F blown away (kinds 19, 34): off the bottom of the screen, -8 health
#   20 hurt and tumbling (kinds 20, 23, deep floor type 0xD; -4 health)
#   21 stage exit (goal line reached, 00D026): walks the exit path
#   22 in a kind 0x16 zone (moves as usual)         23 continue countdown (9 to 0)
#   24 out of the game: message, then 0x0B         25 floor type 8 sequence (sequence_step; shake to escape at step 12)
#   26 pulled by scene_object (20E5F5), thrown, carried with the scroll, then skids
#   27 climbing along an object (kind 26) hand over hand to an x
#   28 swept away in a swirl (kind 30): up off the screen, -8 health
#   29 tripped (kind 31): a hop, then hurt          2A walking in along the stage's entry path (00CFCA)
#   2B game mode 0x18 (stage 0x11, the last): waits for 20E64F (object 01DDF4), +200 rings, then continue countdown
#   2C stuck on a kind 35 object, shake to escape (code not run in the scenarios)
#   2D held by an object of kind 37 (returns at once)
#   2E game over: ranking initials if the rings qualify (08EAC9, 08EC87)

20E646  var  intro_character              s8     # character whose turn it is in the intro (state 0x1E); the first joining player sets it (state 0x34)  (TYPE: FF = none, tested "(int8_t) < 0")
20E669  var  health_setting               u8     # from the settings (20F620, apply_settings 09F6B7): rings per health point (0/4: 1, 1/2: 4, 3: 8) and max health (113EF2)
20E66A  var  starting_health              u8     # from the settings (20F622 & 3 -> 9, 16, 18, 24, table 115B92); object 7E at join
20E66B  var  players_in_play              s8     # 001A7F: players whose player_status is negative (0x81, 0x82, 0xFF)  (TYPE: both readers compare signed, >= 2)
20F062  var  trackball_1_x                s16    # read_controls: movement since last frame (C00040), clamped to +-0x60, negated
20F064  var  trackball_1_y                s16    # read_controls (C00044)
20F066  var  trackball_2_x                s16
20F068  var  trackball_2_y                s16
20F06A  var  trackball_3_x                s16
20F06C  var  trackball_3_y                s16
20F018  var  input_ports                  u32    # read_controls: ports B, A, F, E (active low)
20F01C  var  input_ports_active           u32    # read_controls: ~input_ports
20F020  var  inputs_pressed               u32    # read_controls: newly pressed this frame; bits 0x10/0x18/0x12 trackball buttons 1/2/3 (the jump)
20F024  var  inputs_released              u32    # read_controls: newly released this frame
20F0E2  var  scene_step                   u8     # step of the current stage scene (mode handlers and objects increment it); states 0x18, 0x19 and 0x1C switch on it, 0x25 waits for 2
20E640  var  player_carriers              u16    # [3] object that carries each player off (086B6E registers itself); state 0x31 step 6 moves the player to it
20E62E  var  scene_object                 u16 object    # object the players are pulled to or carried by (states 0x26, 0x30, 0x31); set by 009B4D and stage objects

# ======== stages (from build/naming/stages.txt) ========
# Stages: proposals from the stages helper (symbols.txt syntax, one per line, "# evidence")
# The object sections at the end come from six helpers this helper ran (one per address range), checked
# and adjusted here (names aligned with objects.txt/system.txt/players.txt, game modes written in hex).
#
# How the stage system works (summary; details in the comments below):
# - stage (20F06E) selects 19 slots. Writing cleared_stages makes the protection device set the stage from
#   the order table at 002639 (cleared 0..14 -> 07 06 05 08 09 0A 03 04 10 0C 0D 0E 0F 0B 11) and clear
#   stage_init_flags (20F0BC-20F0BF; MAME: CURRENT_LEVEL_STATUS); the program never writes stage for that.
#   Stage select (game mode 8, slots 00-11) writes stage_select_cleared_values[stage], so its slots 00, 01
#   and 02 come back as 05, 07 and 07 (checked with s32ref: stage_00 and stage_05 both play stage 5,
#   stage_01/_02/_07 all play stage 7). Slot 00 is entered only from inside stage 5: run_stage_05_switch
#   (game mode 0x0A) sets scroll_position 5E5A and stage 0. Slots 01, 02, 12 are never reached. Stage 6
#   (the first after a new game) has no play: its only event is game mode 0x10 (update_stage_06_background),
#   which ends in mode 2.
# - Shared data (per-stage offsets that coincide): stage 7 (the attract demo of game mode 1) reuses stage 3's
#   map (floors, block map, path); 6 reuses 5's; 0E reuses 0C's and 0F reuses 0D's map, path, goal and
#   restart points (only their spawn lists differ); 01, 02, 11 and 12 point at copies of other stages' tables.
#   Stage 9 is the only one whose scroll script starts in mode 0 (it scrolls by itself); the others follow
#   the players (mode 7).
# - game mode 2 = start_stage; game mode 3 = the stage's frame (update_scroll, update_stage_tile_layers,
#   find_nearby_floor_blocks, update_restart_point, the six spawners, check_stage_clear, run_stage_events).
#   run_stage_events switches game_mode to the stage's scripted modes (0x0A-0x1F) at scroll positions:
#   stage 3: 11, 16 at 1B80, 16 at 8610, 15 at A360; 4: 11, 0C; 5: 0A at 100; 6: 10; 8: 0D, 1A at 3100,
#   1C at 7A8D; 9: 13, 14 at 1800, 12 at 4C00; A, C: 11; B: 1F at F00; 10: 11, 19 at C80; 11: 18.
#   Game mode 0x11 opens the screen with update_screen_wipe. A stage ends when the players have walked their
#   exit path past the goal and goal_unlocked is set (an object of each stage sets it: the end machine, the
#   last icicle dropper, goal_unlocker_start...): check_stage_clear goes to 0x17 (stage clear banners), 0x1D
#   (ring tally), 4 (the island map), 2; stages B-F go to 0x1E (a fade straight into the next stage).
#   The only time limit is stage B's escape (game mode 0x1F: 20 seconds once escape_started is set).
# - The camera follows a path made of sections: per section a direction, an end position (in scroll units),
#   x/y limits, a speed and a scroll mode script. scroll_position counts the distance along the path and
#   keys everything: spawn lists, stage events, restart points, the goal.
# - Coordinates: objects have ground x/y (4C/50) and height z (40); project_object turns them into
#   projected coordinates (2A = (x+y)*0.707, 2C = (y-x)*0.354, isometric) and the screen position (0E/0C) is
#   projected - view (view_x/view_y follow the camera).
# - Collision with the map: the stage's floors are boxes (x/y ranges, height, slope, surface kind) in
#   floor_blocks; every frame find_nearby_floor_blocks lists the ones near the view and find_floor
#   gives an object its floor and height. Walls are objects (spawn_walls) that push the players back.
# - Stage objects come from six spawn lists keyed by scroll_position. Most hazards that follow the players
#   are "chasers": a path script of (position or coordinate, screen threshold, catch-up factor, speed,
#   delay) records; behind the threshold they move at max(speed, camera speed * factor >> 8), and they hold
#   back after a player mishap. chaser_object (20E5D4) is the current one (the stage 3 spiked roller, the
#   stage A tornado, the stage B/C fire front, the stage 10 propeller machine...); group leaders, the lava
#   flow, the icicle droppers and the geyser front move the same way.

# ======== Stage flow ========
00075E  func  start_stage                      # game mode 2: cleared_stages+1 (capped at 0E) unless stage_start_kind says not to, clears the stage state, start_stage_view, load_stage_map_pointers, load_stage_goal, find_nearby_floor_blocks, requests stage_start_sounds[stage], game_mode = 3
00196E  func  check_stage_clear                # scroll_position >= goal_scroll_position, 20E593 clear and stage_exit_started set: marks players_finished FF for the players not in play (player_status 0, 2, 3, 4, 82), then needs the u32 at 20E5E0 = FFFFFFFF (the three players_finished bytes and goal_unlocked: a 32-bit read across both variables): game_mode 0x17 (0x1E for stages 0B-0F)
001B74  func  continue_to_next_stage_slot      # when next_stage_slot_request is set: copies two floor_blocks records (stage_link_points), stage++ and load_stage_map_pointers; never runs (20E538 is only ever cleared)
001BED  func  load_stage_map_pointers          # current_restart_point = stage_restart_points[stage]; floor_blocks / floor_block_bounds pointers from 10B6CC / 10E29C
001C31  func  run_stage_events                 # stage_events[stage]: (scroll position, game mode) records; switches game_mode when scroll_position reaches one (within 100)
001CD6  func  update_restart_point             # advances current_restart_point to the last 8-byte record whose position <= scroll_position
001859  func  apply_stage_layer_blending       # stage_layer_blending[stage]: count, then (sprite blend mask, bit, offset from 208000, blend factor word) into the mixer shadows 20F1C0-20F1DE: the layer register gets the mask and the bit (12: blend with sprites, MAME segas32_v), 61004E the factor and enable bit 11
00CFF0  func  load_stage_goal                  # stage_goals[stage]: six u16 -> goal_scroll_position, goal_direction, goal_line, (the fourth is skipped: add.h #2, R12), goal_line_min, goal_line_max
00D026  func  check_player_reached_goal        # past goal_scroll_position and across the goal line (direction 0-3): player state 21 (stage 0: 18; stage 4 waits for goal_unlocked; stage 5 also on object 20E5CA's timer)
00CBAC  func  place_player_at_restart_point    # x/y from the current stage_restart_points record (three kinds), spread by player number; at a stage start (object flag 2000000, in a game) from the 6 bytes before the list
09A5F4  func  load_stage_palette               # stage_palettes[stage]: (source, count) copied to palette RAM at 60B800
016CE3  func  start_stage_view                 # stage != 11: init_stage_view (stage 11 only clears 20CA45)
0158E2  func  init_stage_view                  # display off; tile layer pages, zoom, mixer; the stage's four tile block sets; camera, scroll and section lists from the per-stage tables
01A959  func  move_camera_to_start_section     # load_camera_start_section, then update_camera_view
01A966  func  load_camera_start_section        # like init_stage_view's section setup but from section stage_start_section (attract demos start mid-stage)
016D09  func  run_stage_05_switch              # game mode 0x0A in stage 5: fade out, new tile layers, fade in, then scroll_position = 5E5A and stage = 0
0178AB  func  update_stage_06_background       # game mode 0x10 (stage 6's only event, the scene after a new game; a render shows a player running toward the screen ahead of a big machine with jaws): scripted tile layer and palette steps driven by stage_06_background_step
0968F4  func  update_screen_wipe               # moves four window edges (2090F0-2090FC) to their targets, writes them to 31FF80-31FF86; returns the done bits in R5 (game mode 0x11 waits for 0F)
016EC9  func  update_fade                      # mixer colour offsets 20F1D0-20F1D4 step from/to black or white; fade_kind < 0 when done

20F0BC  var   stage_init_flags      u32        # one bit per once-per-stage setup (bit 0 spawn_objects_by_handler, 2 spawn_ring_rows, 4 spawn_object_groups_2, 5 spawn_walls, 8 run_stage_events, 9 spawn_object_groups, B 001A7F, C 09532E, 6/D/E/10/11 game modes 8/1/17/1B/1D, F/12/13 players 1-3 in 0FFD90/00A85A): set on first run; the protection device clears it (and 20F0BE) with each write to cleared_stages (MAME: CURRENT_LEVEL_STATUS)
20F500  var   stage_order_copy      u16        # boot (00055D) copies stage_order here (11 words); nothing in the program reads it
20E538  var   next_stage_slot_request  u8      # continue_to_next_stage_slot acts on it; the program only clears it
20F0E8  var   stage_start_kind      u8         # start_stage: 0 advances cleared_stages (a new game too: 0 to 1 gives stage 6); stage select sets 1 (no advance); the attract demo path (game mode 0) sets FF: no advance and no player restart
209024  var   stage_start_section   u16        # load_camera_start_section starts the path at this section; start_stage reads it from the attract demo data (+2)
20E5E4  var   goal_scroll_position  u16        # stage_goals[stage]+0; check_stage_clear and check_player_reached_goal wait for scroll_position to reach it
20E5E6  var   goal_direction        u16        # stage_goals+2: which coordinate and side the goal line is crossed on (0-3)
20E5E8  var   goal_line             s16        # stage_goals+4: the x or y the players must cross  (TYPE: check_player_reached_goal compares it signed with object coordinates, 5 of 5 reads)
20E64A  var   goal_line_min         s16        # stage_goals+8: 0 or the start of the goal line on the other axis  (TYPE: signed compares)
20E64C  var   goal_line_max         s16        # stage_goals+A  (TYPE: signed compares)
20F088  var   current_restart_point u32 rom        # pointer into stage_restart_points, moved by update_restart_point; read by place_player_at_restart_point
20E5C6  var   stage_06_shake        u16        # update_stage_06_background step 7: counts down by 80, its high byte shakes the NBG0/NBG3 y scroll
20908F  var   stage_06_background_step  u8     # update_stage_06_background switches on it; game mode 0x10 sets 3 and 5
209088  var   fade_step             u8         # update_fade: 0 start, 1 stepping, 2 done
209089  var   fade_kind             s8         # update_fade: 0 to black, 1 from white, 2 from black, 3 to white; FF when done
20908A  var   fade_delay            u8         # update_fade: frames between steps (1)
20908D  var   fade_delta            u16        # update_fade: added to the three colour offsets each step (+/- fade_speed)
20CA4D  var   fade_speed            u8         # init_stage_view sets 3; update_fade's step size
20908C  var   stage_05_switch_step  s8         # run_stage_05_switch switches on it; FF when done  (TYPE: FF = done, tested signed 4 times, like fade_kind)

002639  table stage_order           u16        # stage per cleared_stages value: 07 06 05 08 09 0A 03 04 10 0C 0D 0E 0F 0B 11; the protection device reads it (MAME: big-endian at 263A, cleared 0 = 7), the program only copies it to stage_order_copy
00265B  table stage_select_cleared_values  u16 # game mode 8 writes [stage] to cleared_stages so that stage_order gives the stage back
002681  table stage_start_sounds    u8         # start_stage (and game mode 1) requests the sound [stage] with 09A5BC
002492  table stage_events          u16        # 19 offsets from 002492 to lists of (u16 scroll position, u8 game mode, u8 0); FFFF ends
002520  table stage_link_points     u16        # 19 offsets from 002520 to two u16 offsets into floor_blocks (continue_to_next_stage_slot)
002694  table stage_layer_blending  u16        # 19 offsets from 002694: u8 count, then 6-byte records (mask, bit, RAM offset of the layer register shadow, blend factor word); used by stages 5, 9, 10
11419A  table stage_goals           u16        # 19 offsets from 11419A to six u16 (load_stage_goal); FFFF position = no goal (stages 0-2, 6, 7, 11, 12)
114B84  table stage_restart_points  u16        # 19 offsets from 114B84 to 8-byte records: u16 scroll position, u8 kind (0/2: u16 x, u16 y at +4; 1: u8 at +3 and two words through 00CC75); the 6 bytes before each list are the stage start (u16 shift that spreads the players, x, y)
10B6CC  table stage_floor_blocks    u16        # 19 offsets from 10B6CC to the stage's floors (load_stage_map_pointers)
10E29C  table stage_floor_block_bounds  u16    # 19 offsets from 10E29C to the stage's floor outlines
108CD0  table stage_palettes        u32        # 19 x (source address, count): load_stage_palette
0026CF  table stage_name_banners    u16        # game mode 0x17: [stage] offset from 0026CF to screen x, screen y and the animation (field 48) of the stage's name banner (stage_clear_banner_reveal; "TRAP TOWER" for stage 3 in a render)

# ======== Scrolling and the camera ========
# update_scroll runs every frame of the stage modes. The scroll mode script (stage_scroll_modes) says what
# the camera does; in modes 7/8 the speed follows the leading player (field 6E of his object).
015F80  func  update_scroll                    # switches on scroll_mode; stops at scroll_end (then stage 3's end sequence); modes 7/8 pick the speed from the players pushing the screen edge
016A77  func  scroll_at_scroll_speed           # scroll mode 0: advance_scroll with scroll_speed
016A7C  func  advance_scroll_unless_ended
016A83  func  advance_scroll                   # move_camera_along_path, then at a section end loads the next section (speed, follow speed, x/y limits, mode script, direction, end)
016B36  func  set_camera_velocity              # camera_velocity_x/_y = section direction * speed; update_camera_with_shake; then update_background_scroll
016B70  func  update_background_scroll         # NBG1/NBG3/NBG2 per-stage scroll; inside stage_fast_scroll_ranges forces follow_base_speed to 10
01699F  func  scroll_slowing_down              # scroll mode 3: scroll_speed - 1 every scroll_mode_duration frames, down to 1
0169CA  func  scroll_speeding_up               # scroll mode 4: scroll_ramp_speed + 1 every scroll_mode_duration frames up to scroll_speed, then mode 0; on the frame the ramp ends (0169FA) it goes on to set the camera velocity with the R3 its caller left (never ran in the scenarios)
016698  func  set_screen_push_edges            # from the section direction: edges 209041-209047 and push_edge_case (which edges count)
016837  func  is_player_facing_scroll          # the player block's angle (field 28, 400 per turn) within a half turn around the scroll direction's quadrant
0168C5  func  is_direction_in_quadrant         # looks for section_direction_y between consecutive sine_table entries of the quadrant set_screen_push_edges chose (4000/C000 count as found)
016267  func  is_player_pushing_edge           # per push_edge_case: R0 = 1 when the player is at the leading edges; a player at the trailing edge sets byte 2 of players_facing_scroll instead
016488  func  is_player_at_diagonal_edge_30     # screen y against screen x / 2 + 30 (and 30 - A); diagonal sections
0164E2  func  is_player_at_diagonal_edge_f0     # screen x against F0 - screen y / 2
016542  func  is_player_at_diagonal_edge_c0
0165A2  func  is_player_at_diagonal_edge_60
0165FC  func  is_player_at_right_edge          # screen x (field 0E) >= push_edge_right; 10 more sets byte 3 of players_facing_scroll
016623  func  is_player_at_left_edge           # screen x <= push_edge_left
01664A  func  is_player_at_top_edge            # screen y (field 0C) <= push_edge_top
016671  func  is_player_at_bottom_edge         # screen y >= push_edge_bottom
017720  func  move_camera_along_path           # camera_x/_y += direction * speed until the section's x/y limits; scroll_position += speed until the section end; jump table by camera_limits_reached
0177FD  func  move_camera_free                 # case 0: advance_camera_scroll_x_y
017800  func  move_camera_at_section_end       # case 1: advance_camera_x_y

017809  func  move_camera_y_done               # case 4: advance_camera_x_scroll

01780F  func  move_camera_xy_done              # case 6: advance_scroll_position

017815  func  advance_camera_scroll_x_y
017828  func  advance_camera_x_y
017835  func  advance_camera_y_scroll
017842  func  advance_camera_y                  # camera_y += section_direction_y * speed

017707  func  update_camera_view_y

# ======== Tile layers (video RAM 300000-31FFFF) ========

0998BC  func  vram_script_set_address          # 80: destination = 300000 + word * 2

0998D0  func  vram_script_skip_long            # A7: destination += s16 * 2

099926  func  vram_script_words_to_dictionary  # 95: like 92, also stores the words in the dictionary at 20F300
09993A  func  vram_script_clear_pages          # 98: address word, page count: clears count * 200 words

099967  func  vram_script_fill_up              # A1: count, word: up a column (-40)
099979  func  vram_script_fill_down_wide       # 9E: count, word: down a column of a 64-cell map (+80)
09998C  func  vram_script_repeat               # A4: count, word: writes the word count times to the same address

# ======== More of the stage flow ========

# update_stage_00_exit_scene for 1B6 + 12C frames, then game mode 2 (stage 8).

01A6E1  func  escape_alarm_flash               # started by 095587 (game mode 0x1F, stage B): while 20E658 (the escape's seconds) is non-zero the green and blue colour offsets swing between 28 and 3F, sound 19 at each end

# ======== Draw list and object removal used by every stage object ========
# The draw list is 100 buckets at 20FA02 (one per screen line, 00-FE from the bottom); the sprite list
# builder walks them every frame, so an object is drawn only on the frames its handler adds it.

# ======== Stage 11 (the ending) and the scripted game modes ========
# (From the stage events helper: renders of s32ref dumps of stage_11 frames 3503-9400, stage_05, stage_06, stage_04, players_2, players_3 and ending.)
# How the ending works (game mode 0x18, stage 11; run_stage_events sets it at scroll 0):
# - update_ending runs every frame: build_ending_scene (step 0 sets up the screen: display off, layer
#   mixing, bitmap layer, vram scripts 171BEB 171C77 17280A 1725B2 1729B2 172A84, sound 94, colour offsets
#   20; step 1 spawns six objects), then floors, restart point, the spawners and the contact checks;
#   joining_closed is held at FF; game over (mode 7) if nobody is in play. start_stage_view clears
#   ending_scene_step for stage 11 instead of running init_stage_view.
# - First scene (frames 3503-4217 in stage_11): the three characters run toward the viewer on a road
#   (scale growing), a tower stands on the horizon behind them; the tower's own timed list
#   (timed_spawns_2, offsets from 01BFC4) fires burning debris arcs from its top, blasts at its base and
#   along the horizon, at 258 the tower collapses (frames 9B00-9B40), a huge explosion and a dust cloud,
#   at 26C the screen flashes to white (second colour offset set up to 1F); then
#   ending_first_scene_done makes the scene objects remove themselves.
# - Credits (4217-8080): ending_credits_fade_in comes back from white and starts the music; the credits
#   spawner (timed_spawns_3, offsets from 01C82F) starts the portrait (Sonic, Ray, Mighty), the name plate
#   with "STARRING" (then Eggman) and seven blocks that scroll up 1 pixel every 2 frames: the team logo
#   and STAFF title, DIRECTOR., PROGRAM., DESIGN., SOUND., VOICE ACTOR., SPECIAL THANKS. (role headings
#   as the renders show them); each block is a sprite plus second-pool parts from its part list.
# - Then the portrait window (clip rectangle 1) opens to the whole screen, fade to black, Eggman flies in
#   with a jet flame and a smoke trail, turns to the viewer, fade, a close-up of his machine flying away
#   into the distance ending in a twinkle, a circle opens (per-line window edges at 30A000/30A400, NBG2
#   pages set), and the three characters run across the screen; 0x78 frames later ending_finished lets the
#   players end the game (player state 2B), game over at 9364 (it prints the "GAME OVER" string record
#   0025D0 instead of 002342 when ending_finished is set).
# The objects keep their own counters in field 30 (byte 0 started, byte 1 a step or done flag, word 32 a
# frame counter) and 60-62 (indexes): per-object scratch, not named.

# ======== Stage 11: scene set-up ========
095177  func  update_ending                     # game mode 0x18 (stage 11): scene_step = FF, next_stage_slot_request 0, joining_closed FF, build_ending_scene, find_nearby_floor_blocks, update_restart_point, the spawners, the contact checks; game mode 7 when player_status is all 0
01BCC6  func  build_ending_scene                # switch on ending_scene_step: 0 display off, set_stage_layer_mixing, clear_sprite_buckets, clear_bitmap_layer, init_video_registers, load_stage_palette_set, queue_sound 94, colour offsets 20, 31FF02 |= 2F, pages and scroll shadows, zoom 200, clip rectangle 1 zero, six run_vram_script calls; 1 allocate_object_outside_loop x6: ending_tower_animate, ending_horizon_show, the three runners, ending_road_scroll; 2/3 nothing
01BF17  func  init_ending_scene_object          # clears field 30 (bytes 30, 31, word 32) of the new object R11 and sets ending_scene_step = 2
20CA45  var   ending_scene_step     u8          # build_ending_scene switches on it (0 screen, 1 objects, 2 done); init_ending_scene_object sets 2; start_stage_view clears it on stage 11
20CA44  var   ending_first_scene_done u8        # build_ending_scene clears it; ending_flash_to_white sets 1 at full white; ending_horizon_show, ending_dust_cloud_rise, ending_road_scroll and animate_ending_runner remove their objects then
20E64F  var   ending_finished       u8          # ending_sonic_run_across sets 1 after 0x78 frames (stage_11 run: frame 9239); start_stage clears it; player state 2B (002CEC, 002FF1) waits for it; game over (run_game_mode 000EE1) then queues the "GAME OVER" string record 0025D0 instead of calling 002342

# ======== Scripted game modes (run_stage_events, cases of run_game_mode) ========
# scene_step (20F0E2, players.txt) is the step of the scripted mode and scene_timer its timer;
# run_stage_events clears both when it switches the mode. Names event_XX_ use the game mode in hex, like
# system.txt's game_mode_event_XX labels. Three modes jump
# through tables of stubs indexed by scene_step (3-byte br for modes 0x0C and 0x0F, 2-byte br for 0x1C); the
# last entry of each table is the step-0 handler itself (09460F, 094888, 095116), reached only if the
# step ran past the end.
20F0E4  var   scene_timer           s16         # timer of the scripted game modes (counts up or down per mode), cleared by run_stage_events; also read by the players (002CEC/002FF1: stage 0 geyser ride while <= 90) and stage 6 objects (084169, 0841DA)

# Not named: 20E5BA (update_stage_05_event step 0 writes 0, nothing reads it) and 20E665 (game mode 0x1F
# step 0 writes 0, nothing reads it); 20E61A is shared (game mode 0x0D, 080160, 0803EB, 084778, 08481D,
# 0890DC, 08924E set or clear it; check_player_jump and player_steer stop the players while it is set):
# probably "player controls locked", left to the players helper.

# ======== Stage objects 080072-0857E4: the chasers (spiked roller) and the objects of stages 3-7 ========
# Stage objects 080072-0857E4 (stage_spawns_by_handler handlers of stages 3-8, B-F and the chaser system)
# Renders: s32ref dumps of walk_03, walk_04, stage_06 (stages 7, 6, 5, 0), stage_0E, plus a frame renderer
# (sprite word + palette from a dump) for the sprites named below.
#
# How the chaser works (080160-080E75):
# - A spiked roller (sprites 5E20-5E60: a gear-shaped cross-section that turns over 9 frames) is built by
#   spiked_roller_start from spiked_roller_kinds[kind]: 5 parts side by side across the path (spacing and
#   direction from spiked_roller_layouts), each with handler spiked_roller_update; the first part is the
#   leader (field 86 of every part), the others copy its x or y (spiked_roller_follow_leader). The leader
#   becomes chaser_object. The parts are on the zone list: kind (field 47) 0C (solid: players are pushed
#   out) until its script starts moving, then 18 (players are hurt even while invulnerable; with flags
#   40000000 an attacking player bounces off along its direction: check_player_contacts), and a back zone
#   object (spawn_roller_back_zone) covers 200 units behind it so nobody can stay behind it.
# - spiked_roller_chase runs the leader's script (10-byte records keyed by scroll_position: screen
#   threshold, catch-up factor, base speed, wait frames): on screen past the threshold it moves at the base
#   speed, else at max(camera speed x factor / 100, base) (catch-up). chaser_speed is the speed (1/16 pixel);
#   the animation speed and a rumble sound (B) follow it. While a player drops in, has a mishap or no player
#   is in play it backs off (waits until it is off screen) for up to FF frames or 300 scroll units.
# - spiked_roller_events (by kind, keyed by scroll_position and a coordinate test) switch the leader to the
#   other states (field 80, jump table at 0803BB).
# - Stage 3: kind 0 at the start (players frozen until it moves; it falls off a ledge near 1B80), kind 1 bursts
#   out of a wall (game mode 0x16 holds the camera until it appears), kind 5 crashes into the machine at 8300
#   (wrecks it; its flame becomes the rising fire), kind 2 drops in near 9B00 and in the finale (game mode
#   0x15) sinks into the stone floor blocks, jumps and lands: the blocks fall and goal_unlocked is set.
#   Stage E: kind 4 rolls into the brick wall (brick_wall_wait bursts). Kind 3 is not spawned by any list.

# ======== Stone floor blocks that crumble at the stage 3 finale (nine at 9C00) ========
080072  func  stage_03_floor_block_start       # stage 3 list at 9C00 (3 x 3 at FA62-FAE9 / 0A79-0B8A, field 04 = kind 0-6): stage_03_floor_block_kinds[kind] gives sprite offsets 64/65, a depth offset (38) and the animation (6780/6770/6778/6798: stone blocks seen in the walk_03 finale renders), field 34 = which stage_03_floor_block_falls byte it waits for; z 0
0800FB  func  stage_03_floor_block_update      # waits until its stage_03_floor_block_falls byte is set, then falls (speed_z += 1000) playing its crumble animation once (6780 -> 6788 -> 6790 rubble); removed below screen y 158
082284  table  stage_03_floor_block_kinds u16  # by kind: offset from 082284 (to 64, 65, depth word, animation) and the fall flag index (kinds 0-2: 0, 3-6: 1)

# ======== Stage objects 0857E5-08A16E: scenery and stages 3, 8, 9, A ========
# Stage objects 0857E5-08A16E (stages 3, 8, 9, A and the shared scenery/script objects), plus 08574A/08576F.
# Renders: s32ref dumps of stage_05 (stage 8),
# a stage 9 walk (gen.py --stage 09 --bias -1 -1 0.8 --seed 2: reaches the end of stage 9), walk_0A and
# walk_03, drawn with render.py and with a per-object renderer that rebuilds each object's sprite entries
# as build_sprite_list does (scratch s89a/objrender.py).
# Touch kinds (field 47) are read through the player's contact switch 00E488: 0x13 and 0x22 (when not
# invulnerable) blow the player away (state 1F), 0x14 hurts with a tumble (state 20), 9/0xC/0x28 hurt
# unless the player is attacking (then he bounces off), 0x1B makes him fall over an edge (state 7, no floor),
# 0x1C sinks him in quicksand (player 114 bit 2), 0x1D is a zone where edges drop at once (player 114 bit 1),
# 0x1E sweeps him away in a swirl (state 28), 0x1F trips him (state 29).
# "Chaser" movement (boulder, lava flow, bridge fire, icicle droppers, tornado, sand block leader): a script
# of records (scroll position and/or a coordinate to reach, then 84 = screen position threshold, 86 = speed
# factor, 88 = minimum speed, 90 = delay); speed = camera ground speed (00AFB3 -> 20E510, or 00B04D ->
# 20E572 with the floor slope) * 86 >> 8, at least 88, and only 88 once the object is past the threshold
# on screen. While no_player_in_play/player_mishap/player_dropping_in (20E599/20E5A3/20E596) are set the
# object holds back (8E = FF, minimum speed 0, threshold moved off screen) for up to 0x300 scroll units.

# ======== Stage objects 08A16E-08DC36 and the group rows 090E49-093E63: stages A-10 ========
# Stage objects 08A16E-08DC36 and row/group objects 090E49-093E63
#
# Common pattern of the chasers and group leaders below (fire front, biting head, rising saws, geyser front,
# waterfall, propeller machine, group_leader_move): a path script of entries (start scroll position or an
# x/y/z limit, a screen-x or screen-y threshold, a catch-up factor, a speed, a delay); while the object is on
# its side of the threshold it moves by the entry's speed, when it falls behind it moves by
# max(speed, camera speed * factor >> 8) (20E510 from 00AFB3, or 20E572 from 00B04D), so it keeps up with
# the screen. The step of the frame is left in chaser_speed (20E556). After a player mishap / a player dropping in / no
# player in play (player_mishap, player_dropping_in, no_player_in_play) it holds just off the screen edge for
# up to FF frames or 300 scroll units.
# Renders: s32ref dumps of tests/controls/walk_0C.txt (stages C, D, E), walk_0A.txt (stage A), and scratch
# copies of walk_0C with the stage poke changed to 10 and 08 and extended to 60000 frames (sb10/walk_10x.txt,
# sb10/walk_08x.txt); sprite frames drawn on their own with sb10/frames.py.

Render walk_0A frame 13500: big sand blocks eaten from one side

# Remaining names: proposals for what build/naming/unnamed.txt (12-10-2026) still lists.
# Syntax as in symbols.txt, one per line, each with "# evidence". Renders: s32ref dumps of
# tests/controls/attract.txt (frames 640-2200) drawn with the stages helper's render.py / frames.py.
#
# Characters: object field 47 (kind) of a player's object is the character it plays: 0 Sonic, 1 Ray,
# 2 Mighty (ranking records, character_name_sprites B728 SONIC / B738 RAY / B730 MIGHTY, the title).
#
# How the pieces named here work (summary; details in the comments):
# - SEGA logo and title (attract system_mode 3): attract_title runs run_title_screen every frame. Until
#   sega_logo_step reaches 7, run_sega_logo plays the SEGA logo (sprite 53D0 + 8n on a temporary second-pool
#   block: fade in from black, zoom in, 1E frames of animation, hold, fade out, 3C frames); then the title scene is
#   built once (title_scene_built): the emblem with Sonic rising out of it and Ray and Mighty popping
#   up (title_emblem_animate), a strip of land sliding in (title_land_slide), clouds drifting up-left and
#   growing (three groups, started by the timed spawner at 097419), a small craft crossing the sky with a
#   smoke trail, and a waving background (per-line scroll of NBG2, palette cycling). title_done after 258 frames.
# - Ranking (attract system_mode 2): start_ranking_display's object scrolls the "TOP 15" screen down,
#   holds 12C frames, then ranking_done. build_ranking_display makes 15 rows of 12 sprites (rank, initials,
#   portrait, name, four score digits, stage reached or ALL CLEAR) and the spinning "TOP15" title.
#   Records (8 bytes): rings (the score), character, stages reached (8 = ALL CLEAR), three letter codes, 0.
#   Letter codes: 00-19 a-z, 20-29 0-9, 2B space (ranking_letter_sprites).
# - Ranking entry (player state 2E): start_ranking_entry checks the player's rings against the lowest
#   record and sets up a static block (ranking_entry_blocks, outside the object pools) that
#   enter_ranking_initials runs: 3 letters chosen with the trackball, 20-second countdown, or OUT OF RANK!
# - Character select at the start of a game (game mode 0x1B, player state 34): start_character_chooser
#   makes the PLAYER SELECT heading with its countdown (character_select_countdown_update) and one chooser
#   per player: the character turns with the trackball x (character_chooser_turn), the button or the end of
#   character_select_timer confirms (character_chooser_confirm: voice, the character goes into the player
#   object's kind). Joining later (player_select_character): start_join_character_chooser shows a small
#   portrait with a 9-second countdown (join_character_chooser_update). characters_taken holds one bit per
#   character already playing.
# - Camera speed helpers for the chasers: compute_camera_ground_speed (flat) and
#   compute_camera_slope_speed (R8 = the floor slope factor) turn camera_velocity_x/_y into a ground speed
#   and direction, recomputed only when the velocity (or slope) changed.
# - Grey screen: update_grey_screen (every stage frame) greys the four tile layers (mixer 3E bits 1-4:
#   MAME's grayscale colour offset mode) while any player block's 9F is set, and some objects switch to
#   grey palettes (arrow_board_ride, crumbling_floor_update) or stop (group_leader_move, spiked_roller_chase). Nothing ever sets
#   player field 9F: the effect is dormant.
#
# Mirrors: rom_0FF08C/0FF08E and rom_0FFFCE-0FFFE0 are reads of 09F08C/09FFCE-09FFE0 through the 0FFxxx
# mirror (the code at 09Fxxx runs there). 09F08C is already rom_checksums: the names below are only needed if
# table reads are not folded to 09Fxxx (the decompiler does not fold them today).

# Not proposed: player 02, 2A and 47 (and the shadow_update uses of 54 and 58) are not player fields:

field player 54 drift_turned_back u8        # state 26 (pulled, then carried with the scroll): 0 when the carried phase starts, FF once x >= CD0; then the drift turns to 300 (scroll_drift_direction) and the phase ends back at x <= 630 (player_state_pulled 008E31-008EB0, player_move_with_scroll)

# ---------------- scoped object fields (7E-9F, per handler family) ----------------
# Format: "# scoped object FAMILY_PREFIX OFFSET NAME TYPE  # evidence". The names describe the fields of the
# object the family's code runs on (OBJECT(current_object)); inside these functions some lines touch other
# objects' fields at the same offsets (children being set up, the touched object, the parent), which these
# names do not describe: e.g. handle_rod_init sets its handles' 80-94, machine_fire_update its fireballs'
# 7F/96/9C, player_stuck_wait_release reads the holder's 80. Where a family's parts share the prefix with a
# different layout, the parts get a longer prefix that should win (burning_boulder_flame over
# burning_boulder, handle_rod_handle / handle_rod_post over handle_rod, group_leader_move / group_leader_hold,
# icicle_update / icicle_cracks / icicle_shadow instead of icicle, which would also take icicle_dropper).
# Most used families first. Not done (meanings change between the family's own handlers, or too little
# use): eel, snow_mound, sand_rock, rock_wall, spike_panel, saw_blade, opening_machine, flame_machine_*,
# eggman_scene, ember_emitter, crawler, centipede, whirlwind and the small effect objects.
#
# The chaser movement (fire front, biting head, sand block leader, propeller machine, waterfall, rising saws,
# lava flow, geyser front, bridge fire, machine fire, icicle droppers, burning boulder): one routine copied
# into each handler. A path script record gives a position or coordinate to reach, then (threshold, catch-up
# factor, base speed, wait); on its side of the threshold the object moves at the base speed, behind it at
# max(base, camera_ground_speed (or camera_slope_speed) x factor >> 8); chaser_speed gets the step. After a
# player mishap / a player dropping in / no player in play it holds back (threshold moved off screen, base
# speed 0) for FF frames or 300 scroll units.
# fire_front (fire_front_init, fire_front_chase): the chaser movement
scoped object fire_front 80 path u32 rom  # next record of its path script (the record's words are loaded into 84/86/88/90 when its position or coordinate is reached)
scoped object fire_front 84 screen_threshold s16  # screen coordinate it compares its own with: on its side it moves at base_speed, behind it at max(base_speed, camera speed x catch_up_factor >> 8)
scoped object fire_front 86 catch_up_factor u16  # multiplies the camera's ground speed (>> 8) when it falls behind
scoped object fire_front 88 base_speed s16  # speed of the current record (chaser_speed when it is ahead)
scoped object fire_front 8A saved_threshold s16  # screen_threshold kept while holding back (a player mishap / dropping in / no player in play)
scoped object fire_front 8C saved_base_speed s16  # base_speed kept while holding back (base_speed is 0 meanwhile)
scoped object fire_front 8E holding_back u8  # FF while it holds back
scoped object fire_front 8F hold_timer u8  # FF frames of holding back at most (always FF without players in play)
scoped object fire_front 90 wait_timer s16  # frames of the record's wait: it does not move until 0
scoped object fire_front 92 hold_start_position u16  # scroll_position when it started holding back: it gives up after 300 units

# biting_head (biting_head_init, biting_head_wait, biting_head_chase): the chaser movement
scoped object biting_head 80 path u32 rom  # as fire_front 80 (the same chaser code)
scoped object biting_head 84 screen_threshold s16  # as fire_front 84 (the same chaser code)
scoped object biting_head 86 catch_up_factor u16  # as fire_front 86 (the same chaser code)
scoped object biting_head 88 base_speed s16  # as fire_front 88 (the same chaser code)
scoped object biting_head 8A saved_threshold s16  # as fire_front 8A (the same chaser code)
scoped object biting_head 8C saved_base_speed s16  # as fire_front 8C (the same chaser code)
scoped object biting_head 8E holding_back u8  # as fire_front 8E (the same chaser code)
scoped object biting_head 8F hold_timer u8  # as fire_front 8F (the same chaser code)

# ---- text map: erase_text_list, print_formatted_text and its eraser ----
# A formatted text: a position word (text map offset, 31F000 | word), an attribute byte, then runs of characters ending
# in 0, each followed by a code byte that jumps through a table of 3-byte branches right after the run's loop (0996A7,
# 099703, 099764 to print; 0997BC, 0997FD, 099841 to erase): 0 end; 3/6/9 next run at 1/2/3 cells per character;
# C new attribute byte, same width; F/15/1B new position word and attribute byte at width 1/2/3; 12/18/1E new
# attribute byte at width 1/2/3; 21 skip s8 cells, 24 skip s16 cells (same width). Width 2 writes cell, cell + 1;
# width 3 cell, cell + 1, cell + 2 (a character drawn as 2 or 3 consecutive tiles). The eraser walks the same
# records writing R0 (0) and skipping the attribute bytes; its tables have no entry 24 (it would land inside 21's code).

# dead_work_4: 09B382-09BC7E, the unused part of the bitmap-layer drawing library (draw_line and fill_rect are the live part, used by test mode):
# a filled quadrilateral, a circle drawn as 64 lines, a midpoint circle (4 and 8 bpp, clipped) and a scanline flood fill

09B382  func  fill_quad                 # unused: fills the quadrilateral R0,R1 / R2,R3 / R4,R5 / R6,R7 (vertices in order round it, convex) with colour R8 on the 8 bpp bitmap layer: sorts the vertices by y (key y << 8 | vertex number), walks the left and right edges in 16.16 into the span list at 20B500 (bitmap address, length per row) and draws it with 09B30F; flat cases go to fill_span_8bpp (one row) or the triangle code 09B1C4/09B27E (three vertices on one row). Keeps the vertices on the stack (stack_pointer) to find the bottom vertex's neighbours
09B963  func  draw_circle_polygon       # unused: circle of radius |R2| around R0,R1 in colour R3 as 64 points (8 steps of sine_table/cosine_table x radius >> 14, mirrored into 8 octants) at 20B500 (x, y pairs), then draw_line between them; buggy: two mirrored stores use displacements 7E[R13] and 7F[R11] (-82 and 7E fit), and the line loop steps the list 2 bytes at a time (x, y and y, next x as the ends), so it would not draw a circle
09BA54  func  draw_circle               # unused: midpoint circle of radius |R2| around R0,R1 in colour R3, 8 points per step (plot_circle_point_4bpp/_8bpp by bitmap_8bpp); returns at once when the circle is wholly outside bitmap_window, and R18 (current_player in C) carries a 2-bit-per-point mask of the octants that need the window test (bit 1 draw unclipped, bit 0 test); the masks assume the points in order round the circle, but points 4, 6 and 7 are plotted in another order
09BC03  func  plot_circle_point_4bpp    # unused (draw_circle): R18 << 1 twice: top bit = plot without the window test, next bit = plot if R0,R1 is inside bitmap_window (R14-R17); at 4 bpp: (y << 8) + (x >> 1) + R12, odd x into the high nibble (R2), even into the low (R3)
09BC53  func  plot_circle_point_8bpp    # unused (draw_circle): the same at 8 bpp: byte R3 at (y << 9) + x + R12
09BC7E  func  flood_fill                # unused: scanline flood fill from R0,R1 with colour R2 up to border colour R3, inside bitmap_window (nothing when the seed is outside or already R2/R3): 09BD99 fills the seed's span, then a ring queue of 26-byte span records at 20B500-20CCC3 (written through R23, read through R24, both pushed; object_cursor/last_object in C) is worked off with 09BF99 (rows above and below); the queue overlaps string_queue and the test variables at 20C800-20CA4F

# --- Flood fill of the bitmap layer (span fill with a queue of spans at 20B500-20CCC4) ---
# flood_fill (dead_work_4) is the entry: R0/R1 seed point, R2 fill colour, R3 border colour; it fills the
# seed's span, then takes 0x1A-byte span records from the queue (R24 = last_object reads, R23 = object_cursor
# writes, both saved and restored) until it is empty.
09BD58  func  flood_fill_push_span              # unused: flood_fill_span from R10/R14 in row R11 + R9, then queues its record (R9, row, right x/address, left x/address, the flood_fill_push_parent_* range) at R23, wrapping from 20CCC4 to 20B500
09BD99  func  flood_fill_span                   # unused: from the pixel at R10 (x) / R14 (address) scans left to R4 and right to R6 until the fill colour (R12 low byte) or the border colour (R3), fills the run with R12 (bytes, then words, 16 at a time); R10/R14 come back as its left end, R16/R15 its right end; also fill_span_at_point's 8bpp path
09BEBB  func  flood_fill_scan_seed_rows         # unused: the seed span's neighbour rows: flood_fill_scan_row above (R9 = -1) when y > window top (R5), below (R9 = 1) when y < window bottom (R7)
09BECE  func  flood_fill_scan_row               # unused: walks row y + R9 under/over the current span (flood_fill_left_x..right_x); every run not yet in the fill or border colour goes through flood_fill_push_span, flood_fill_push_parent_left_x moving past it
09BF99  func  flood_fill_scan_span_rows         # unused: the same as flood_fill_scan_seed_rows for a span taken from the queue (flood_fill_scan_row_skip_parent)
09BFAC  func  flood_fill_scan_row_skip_parent   # unused: R9 = the span's own direction (flood_fill_direction): the whole next row (flood_fill_scan_row); back toward its parent: only the parts left of flood_fill_parent_left_x and right of flood_fill_parent_right_x + 1
09C10D  func  fill_span_at_point                # unused: R0,R1 point (get_point_outcode: nothing outside bitmap_window), R2 fill colour, R3 border colour: the one horizontal run through the point. 8bpp: flood_fill_span. 4bpp: nibble scans, but R10 still holds the outcode (never set to x) and R15 is never set: that path cannot work as written

# The flood fill queue records (0x1A bytes) as flood_fill_push_span writes them through R23 (object_cursor)
struct flood_fill_record 1A                     # one span the unused flood_fill queues (ring of them at 20B500-20CCC3, written through R23, read through R24)
field flood_fill_record 00 direction_and_y u16  # low byte the direction (R9), high byte the row (R11 + R9): popped into flood_fill_direction/flood_fill_y
field flood_fill_record 02 right_x u16  # flood_fill_span's R16
field flood_fill_record 04 right_address u32  # flood_fill_span's R15
field flood_fill_record 08 left_x u16  # flood_fill_span's R10
field flood_fill_record 0A left_address u32  # flood_fill_span's R14
field flood_fill_record 0E parent_right_x u16  # flood_fill_push_parent_right_x
field flood_fill_record 10 parent_right_address u32  # flood_fill_push_parent_right_address
field flood_fill_record 14 parent_left_x u16  # flood_fill_push_parent_left_x
field flood_fill_record 16 parent_left_address u32  # flood_fill_push_parent_left_address
